newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates, spots end mostly up.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates, spots end mostly up.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mostly up on Wednesday due to increased demand of funds because of listings of three new domestic stocks in Shanghai today, traders said.
The annual rate for the most active 14-day contract rose to 18.00 percent from 15.50 percent on Tuesday.
Total turnover fell to 5.08 million lots from 11.04 million. One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
"Most institutions absorbed funds from the repo market to trade the new shares, pushing up the rates," said one trader.
"The 14-day became the most active contract today mainly because its rate was comparatively low," he added.
Three domestic A share companies, Xinhua Metal Industrial Co, Si Sha Co and Lu Yin Industrial (Group) Co, made their debuts on the Shanghai stock exchange today.
Traders expect the repo rates to have a technical correction in the next two days.
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mostly up on a technical rebound after successive falls in the past few days but market sentiment remained bearish, traders said.
The most active 10-year bond that matures in June 2006 ended up at 115.87 yuan from 115.65 yuan.
Combined volume of the nine-contract market increased to 1.18 million lots from 898,514 lots.
"The rise was slight and the market sentiment was still weak," said one trader.
Traders expect the contracts to resume their downward trend in the next few days due to the weak sentiment.
